description: The eoPortal Satellite Missions catalogue is a database of articles about past, operational and future spaceborne Earth observation missions and sensors, and about other space missions. Each mission article opens with quick facts (mission type, agency, launch date and end-of-life date) and then describes the spacecraft, launch, mission status, sensor complement and references; for example, the LMRST-Sat article covers a NASA-JPL and Stanford CubeSat that tested an X-band transponder for Deep Space Network calibration, launched in October 2015. It is global in scope and can be filtered between Earth observation and other missions, with each article showing its last update date. The site is operated by the European Space Agency, and its terms state that ESA does not guarantee the accuracy of information from external sources. Articles are free to read on the web without an account; no reuse licence is stated in the terms read. Caveats: articles are narrative and of uneven currency, so values need checking against operators, and there is no bulk download. It helps modellers describe satellites and their payloads when building space segment inventories for hazard exposure and resilience studies; a related record is the UCS satellite database.
